name: PostEDA-Bench
description: PostEDA-Bench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM-based agents on post-EDA (Electronic Design Automation) tasks for digital integrated-circuit design. It contains 145 tasks organized into two sub-benchmarks: (1) DRC-Bench, which evaluates an agent's ability to interpret and reason about Design Rule Check violations on ASAP7 GDS layouts (drc_essential: 40 tasks across 3 difficulty levels; drc_reasoning: 30 tasks across 3 difficulty levels); and (2) PPA-Bench, which evaluates an agent's ability to optimize Power, Performance, and Area of OpenROAD synthesis/place-and-route flows (ppa_mono: 35 single-objective tasks across area/performance/power, with performance covering 3 difficulty levels and area/power covering 2; ppa_multi: 40 multi-objective tasks across 2 difficulty levels). Each task ships with a natural-language prompt, fully reproducible OpenROAD configuration, RTL/Verilog source, GDS layouts, reports, and a hidden ground-truth/evaluation harness. Submissions are evaluated by closed-form scripts that re-run the EDA flow and compare against held-out targets.

citeAs: @inproceedings{posteda_bench_2026, title={PostEDA-Bench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents on Post-EDA Design Closure Tasks}, author={Anonymous Authors}, booktitle={Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) Datasets and Benchmarks Track}, year={2026}, note={Anonymized for double-blind review}}
rai:dataCollection: Tasks were authored by the dataset creators using open-source EDA tooling. DRC tasks were generated by running ASAP7 DRC runsets via KLayout on a curated set of GDS layouts (synthesized from open-source RTL such as OpenROAD-flow-scripts demo designs and self-authored sequence detectors), then programmatically injecting controlled DRC violations and capturing the violation reports. PPA tasks were generated by running the OpenROAD-flow-scripts (ORFS) flow end-to-end on open-source RTL designs at the ASAP7 7nm node, recording the resulting Power, Performance, and Area metrics, and then setting target values that require non-trivial optimization to meet. Each task was manually reviewed for solvability, difficulty calibration (L1/L2/L3), and uniqueness.
rai:dataCollectionType: Programmatic generation from open-source EDA flows
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-source RTL (Verilog) for digital designs; the public ASAP7 7nm Process Design Kit (PDK) and DRC runsets; OpenROAD-flow-scripts (ORFS) configuration files. No third-party proprietary IP, no human-subject data, and no scraped web data are included.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: None. Each of the 145 tasks contains the complete set of artifacts required for execution and grading (prompt.txt, info.json with hidden ground truth, and supporting EDA inputs such as GDS, RTL, ORFS configs, reports, and logs).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: GDS files were normalized to a single top cell and re-flattened where necessary so that DRC reports are deterministic. OpenROAD flow runs were re-executed with fixed random seeds and pinned tool versions to ensure metric reproducibility. Hidden evaluation targets (ground-truth DRC violation lists and PPA target thresholds) were extracted into per-task info.json files and excluded from the LLM-visible prompt context.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each task was annotated with: (a) a difficulty label (L1, L2, L3, or single/multi-objective for PPA) determined by the number of independent constraints and the size of the design space; (b) a ground-truth answer (DRC violation set or PPA target metrics) computed by deterministic open-source EDA tools rather than human judgement; (c) a natural-language prompt written in English by the dataset authors and peer-reviewed within the team for clarity and absence of leakage. Annotators were the dataset creators, who hold graduate-level expertise in VLSI/EDA.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Annotation, ground-truth generation, and review were performed using local scripts (Python, Bash) and the open-source tools KLayout (DRC) and OpenROAD-flow-scripts (PPA). No commercial annotation platform or crowdsourcing was used.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Ground-truth labels are deterministic outputs of open-source EDA tools (KLayout DRC and OpenROAD synthesis/PnR), so inter-annotator agreement is not applicable to the labels themselves. Prompt clarity and task solvability were cross-reviewed by at least two team members per task, and tasks were sanity-checked end-to-end by running a strong baseline agent (a frontier LLM with tool-use) and confirming that the task is non-trivial yet solvable in principle.
rai:dataAnnotationPerItem: Each task has exactly one ground-truth evaluation specification, computed deterministically by EDA tools, and reviewed by at least two members of the dataset team.
rai:dataAnnotationDemographics: Not applicable. Tasks involve only digital-circuit artifacts (GDS, RTL, EDA reports). No human-subject data is collected, so demographic information of annotators or subjects is not relevant to the data itself.
rai:dataAnnotationTools: OpenROAD / OpenROAD-flow-scripts (synthesis, place, route, PPA extraction)
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: (1) benchmarking LLM-based agents (single-call, ReAct, Reflexion, Tree-of-Thought, proposer-critic, ORFS-agent, etc.) on realistic post-EDA design closure tasks; (2) studying tool-use, planning, and multi-step reasoning on long-horizon engineering workflows; (3) evaluating progress on agentic AI for chip design. Out-of-scope uses: production-grade tape-out sign-off, drawing conclusions about commercial PDKs (only ASAP7 academic PDK is used), and any safety-critical hardware verification.
rai:dataBiases: PostEDA-Bench reflects the conventions, design styles, and tool defaults of the open-source EDA ecosystem (OpenROAD, ASAP7, KLayout). Models or agents trained or tuned on similar open-source data may have an advantage; conversely, agents specialized for proprietary commercial EDA flows (e.g., Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA) may underperform even if substantively capable. The benchmark covers only the ASAP7 7nm node and a finite set of digital RTL designs, and therefore does not reflect the diversity of analog/mixed-signal, advanced-node FinFET/GAA, or 3D-IC design flows.
rai:dataLimitations: Task counts are modest (50 tasks total) and all tasks share a single PDK (ASAP7) and a single open-source flow (OpenROAD). PPA targets are calibrated against a particular tool version; small changes in tool versions may shift baseline metrics by a few percent. Some tasks require running OpenROAD locally, which can take minutes per evaluation and is gated by environment setup. Performance on this benchmark should not be extrapolated to claim general 'chip-design ability' without further evidence on additional nodes, designs, and flows.
rai:dataSensitive: None. All artifacts are derived from open-source RTL, the academic ASAP7 PDK, and open-source EDA tools. The dataset contains no personal data, no commercially sensitive IP, no security-relevant secrets (no cryptographic keys, no proprietary masks), and no data subject to export-control regulations beyond what already applies to publicly released ASAP7 collateral.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains no personal data and no sensitive personal information. It contains only digital integrated-circuit design artifacts (Verilog, GDS, EDA configuration files, EDA logs and reports) and natural-language task prompts authored by the dataset team.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive impact: PostEDA-Bench standardizes evaluation of LLM agents for chip-design automation, lowering the bar for reproducible research and helping the community track real progress on agentic AI for EDA. Potential negative impact: improved AI-driven EDA could affect employment patterns of junior chip-design engineers; we mitigate this by releasing under a permissive open license and emphasizing that current SOTA agents remain far from human-expert performance on the harder L3 / multi-objective tasks. The benchmark itself does not enable any new misuse beyond what is already possible with open-source EDA tooling.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioned releases are tagged (current: 1.0.0). Bug fixes, additional tasks, and PDK/tool-version refreshes will be released as minor versions; breaking changes (e.g., re-calibration of PPA targets) trigger a major-version bump. Issues, errata, and discussion are tracked in the project's public issue tracker (URL to be finalized at camera-ready). The maintainers commit to at least 24 months of active maintenance from the date of publication. Mirror copies will be deposited on a long-term archival service (Zenodo) to ensure persistence.
rai:syntheticDataGeneration: Portions of PostEDA-Bench are programmatically generated rather than collected from naturally occurring sources, so we mark `hasSyntheticData` as true. Specifically: (1) DRC violation reports are produced by running KLayout against ASAP7 DRC runsets on GDS layouts; for some DRC-Reasoning tasks the violations are deliberately induced by controlled perturbations of the layout (e.g., shifting cells, scaling shapes) to create well-defined error patterns. (2) PPA target metrics (area / clock period / power thresholds) are derived programmatically from baseline OpenROAD-flow-scripts runs and then tightened by the dataset authors so that the optimization task is non-trivial. The underlying RTL designs and the ASAP7 PDK are real, open-source artifacts, not synthetic; only the violation patterns and the optimization targets are programmatically constructed. No generative AI / LLM-produced content is included in the dataset.

recordSet.name: drc_essential
recordSet.description: DRC-Essential split: 15 tasks asking the agent to identify, count, and categorize Design Rule Check violations on ASAP7 GDS layouts. 3 difficulty levels x 5 questions each.

field.name: prompt
field.description: Natural-language task prompt presented to the agent under evaluation. The corresponding GDSII input layout lives next to each prompt.txt file (top_cell.gds) and is declared as the 'drc-essential-gds' FileSet in distribution.

recordSet.name: drc_reasoning
recordSet.description: DRC-Reasoning split: 15 tasks requiring multi-step reasoning over DRC violations (root-cause attribution, hierarchy traversal, fix planning). 3 difficulty levels x 5 questions each.

field.name: prompt
field.description: Natural-language task prompt. The corresponding GDSII input layout lives next to each prompt.txt file (top_cell.gds) and is declared as the 'drc-reasoning-gds' FileSet in distribution.

recordSet.name: ppa_mono
recordSet.description: PPA-Mono split: 35 single-objective Power/Performance/Area optimization tasks on OpenROAD-flow-scripts at ASAP7. The agent must edit OpenROAD configs, SDC, or RTL to meet a specific target (area-only, perf-only, or power-only). Difficulty: L1, L2 for area and power; L1, L2, L3 for perf.

field.name: task_id
field.description: Unique identifier of the form 'ppa_mono/<objective>/L<level>/q<index>' where objective in {area, perf, power}.

field.name: objective
field.description: Single PPA objective being optimized: 'area', 'perf', or 'power'.

field.name: prompt
field.description: Natural-language task prompt stating current and target metric values.

recordSet.name: ppa_multi
recordSet.description: PPA-Multi split: 40 multi-objective tasks where the agent must jointly satisfy multiple PPA constraints (e.g., meet a tighter clock period while keeping power below a budget) on ASAP7 / OpenROAD-flow-scripts. Difficulty: L1, L2.

field.name: prompt
field.description: Natural-language task prompt stating current values and multiple target constraints.
